thread:
maria: quick heads-up — after the allocator change merged in PR #4321, perf lab shows higher prefix cache fragmentation and increased eviction churn. can someone run a focused smokecheck on compaction and slot reuse? :thinking:
jon: on it. which workload waveform should I use? the standard long-tail sim or the real-world trace from customer-x?
maria: start with customer-x trace (it's the one that regressed). then run the long-tail sim if you see anything unclear. look for increased free-slab counts and lots of small fragments.
jon: copying the command I'm running:
```
./tools/kv-prof --cluster=perf-lab-4 --trace=customer-x-2026-03-10.trace --out=job_1976_frag.json --scan-prefix=true --compact-pass=2
```
lee: FYI I pushed a tiny allocator tweak today that changes arena split thresholds (opt-in behind env var KV_ARENA_AGGRESSIVE=1). could that explain it?
maria: yup that's the suspect. jon, please run with env both on and off. also collect per-shard histograms for slot sizes.
jon: running both now, ETA ~12m. I'll post the compact-pass samples and a tiny grep of suspicious lines.
ci-bot: CI pipeline triggered: job/kv-smoke-1976543210 (running). logs: https://ci.redwood.dev/jobs/1976543210 :gear:
olivia: if we see a lot of ~64B fragments that suggests the new split threshold is too low. earlier experiments showed a 3x increase in 32/64B bucket occupancy under certain seqlen distributions.
sarah: note that the cache eviction policy recently got a small change to prefer older prefixes on tie. that could interact with hole creation. @lee can you comment?
lee: correct — tie-breaker changed in d0f3b7. I think it's orthogonal but possible it exposes fragmentation upstream. I can revert if we confirm allocator is the root.
jon: quick grep from job_1976_frag.json (both runs):
```
RUN: KV_ARENA_AGGRESSIVE=0 -> small_fragments: 412, eviction_ops: 1203
RUN: KV_ARENA_AGGRESSIVE=1 -> small_fragments: 1743, eviction_ops: 3890
TOP_SIZES: 32B=61%, 64B=24%, 128B=10%
```
maria: whoa that's a clear delta. can you also capture a hotset sample (top 500 prefixes) and check if hotset shifted or if many prefixes were evicted then reloaded?
jon: capturing hotset now and will diff. also running a baseline with the old allocator commit for sanity.
olivia: while that's running, suggest adding a quick 1-min compaction-only job to see if a more aggressive compaction pass reduces small fragments. maybe the split decision is fine if compaction reclaims quickly.
sarah: agree. adding compaction-only helps isolate whether fragmentation is transient.
jon: posted results: https://perf.redwood.dev/runs/1976543210 — diff shows 3.1x uptick in 32/64B fragments with aggressive arena, and hotset churn increased by ~2.2x. compaction-only reduced fragments by ~40% but not to baseline.
maria: thanks. conclusion: allocator change increases fragment creation; compaction helps but doesn't fully close gap. next steps: revert opt-in change, open an alternative approach in PR #4330 that tweaks split heuristics (larger min-slab) and add a compact-after-split flag. @lee can you take PR #4330?
lee: yup I'll pick it up today. will prototype and post perf numbers.
maria: awesome. once PR is up, please tag me and @sarah for a quick review. also add a short regression smoke in the perf lab pipeline to catch this before rollout.
deploy-bot: reminder — no deploys to perf-lab-4 until the regression is triaged. (auto-lock applied)
jon: thanks team, closing loop once PR perf numbers are in. :thumbsup:
